findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or repository access can retrieve these credentials and use them directly.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so environment variables (which here contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext to any principal that can describe the function. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would provide an additional access control boundary.

The function uses nodejs12.x, a runtime that has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime and its bundled OpenSSL/system libraries unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary. Combined with the embedded static AWS credentials, a compromise of the function code allows unconstrained exfiltration to arbitrary external endpoints.
